name: The Jargon-to-Human Dictionary
why_it_works: Industry jargon makes people feel shut out. A mock dictionary that gives the stiff official definition and then the honest human one makes viewers laugh with relief and feel smarter, and it positions the brand as the translator on their side. People save and share 'finally someone said it' slides.

hook.pattern: Promise to translate the words your industry uses to confuse people, in dictionary format.
examples: What your {{industry}} pro says vs. what they mean.
A dictionary for every {{industry}} word that made you nod politely.

craft.technique: Mock dictionary: official vs. human definition (incongruity) with a self-own bonus
craft.notes: Setup: the dictionary format and the stiff 'Official:' line on every slide set up a formal pattern. Turn: each 'Human:' line breaks the formality with an honest, slightly cheeky meaning, and it ends on an unexpected small comparison (paper towels, romance) as the punch word. Tag: the bonus slide turns the joke on the brand itself with a made-up internal word, which is the self-deprecating tag that earns trust. Timing in a carousel lives in the swipe: put the punch word as the very last words on each slide so the 'pause' is the moment before the next swipe, and keep the 'Official:' lines short so the reader gets to the turn fast.

do_not: Make a 'human' definition inaccurate just to get a laugh; it must still be correct
Joke about people who didn't know the word; the joke is on the jargon
Use more than three real terms before the bonus slide
Give personalized advice in a definition
compliance: Mortgage: definitions are general education, not a rate offer; no rate, payment or approval promises; show NMLS ID and Equal Housing Opportunity on the end card
Law firms: definitions are general information, not legal advice; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires
Financial advisors: no return or performance claims inside any definition; include required firm disclosures in the caption
Insurance: definitions must not imply any specific coverage; add 'coverage varies by policy and state'
Have a licensed professional at the business check every definition for accuracy before posting
